newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African police arrest three in corruption case.
newsitem.headline: S.African police arrest three in corruption case.

text.p: South African police said on Monday they had arrested two interpreters and a court clerk over the theft of a charge sheet which they had planned to sell to the accused in the case for 5,000 rand ($1,075).

Police said in a statement the men were arrested after a "sting" operation carried out by officers in an anti-corruption unit, acting on information given to them. The court charge sheet related to a drugs case.
The two interpreters were employed by two separate firms of lawyers as interpreters in Kempton Park east of Johannesburg, while the clerk worked at the Kempton Park Magistrate's Court.
The men are due to appear in court on Tuesday, after a failed bail attempt late on Friday soon after the arrests. Police said their investigations were continuing, and gave no further details.
Crime is one of President Nelson Mandela government's most urgent priorities. Police figures show 5,863 murders were reported around the country from January to March this year.
